questions.q: What does a recipient's Delta Sharing client actually call to list shares and get access to files?
options: The provider's internal notebook API
A direct SQL connection to the provider's cluster
A proprietary Databricks-only binary protocol
An open, documented REST API exposed by a Delta Sharing Server
questions.explain: Delta Sharing is built on an open REST protocol — the client lists shares/tables, gets metadata, and gets pre-signed URLs to read Parquet files.

questions.q: Why can a non-Databricks client (plain Python, Power BI) read a Delta-shared table at all?
options: Non-Databricks clients cannot actually read shared tables
Databricks provides a free, hidden Databricks account to every recipient automatically
The shared table is converted to CSV before being sent
Delta Sharing is an open protocol — the client only needs to speak REST and read Parquet, neither of which requires Databricks
questions.explain: Because the underlying protocol is open and documented, any compatible client can participate, not just Databricks-native ones.

questions.q: What is the key difference between Databricks-to-Databricks sharing and open sharing?
options: There is no functional difference between the two
Databricks-to-Databricks sharing surfaces the shared table directly in the recipient's own Unity Catalog with no credential file; open sharing issues a credential file for non-Databricks clients
Databricks-to-Databricks sharing requires exporting the table to CSV first
Open sharing is only available within the same cloud region
questions.explain: The recipient's side of the exchange differs significantly depending on whether they also run Unity Catalog.

questions.q: What does adding a table to a share WITH HISTORY enable?
options: It converts the share into a Databricks-to-Databricks share automatically
It permanently deletes older versions of the table
It disables governance (masks/row filters) on the shared table
The recipient can read the table's version history and Change Data Feed, pulling incremental changes instead of re-reading the whole table
questions.explain: History-aware sharing lets a recipient track changes over time via CDF rather than only ever seeing the current snapshot.

questions.q: What is the real technical distinction between Delta Sharing and simply exporting a file to a partner?
options: Delta Sharing requires the recipient to manually copy files every day
Exporting a file is always faster than any form of Delta Sharing
There is no real difference — both approaches are functionally identical
Delta Sharing can expose the table's live version history and incremental changes through an open protocol, not just a static current snapshot
questions.explain: Sharing with history moves beyond a one-time export by giving the recipient ongoing, incremental access through the same protocol.
